title: Recorder
summary: Measured, and worse (2026-11-08): the pages now carry four measured values in place of a fitted scale and three estimates, and every note fell about 64 cents (57.3 to 70.5): the held F4 and A4 now sound -64.8 and -91.7 cents of equal temperament on A = 440, the scale and melody -36.3 to -91.8. The longer bore accounts for 43 cents of the fall (the passive first modes fall 42.92 to 43.00 cents); the remaining 14.3 to 27.5 cents is not separated among the jet's convection speed, the vena contracta and the windway height, which changed together. Against Bouterse's own readings of this alto in a 15 C room, moved to this scale, the pages sit 31.5 to 57.8 cents flat (F4 held 50.0, A4 held 56.9, Bb4 of the scale 31.5, B4 crescendo at 400 Pa 57.8). The gas in the bore is breath at 27 C; whether a played recorder's bore sits at 27 C or nearer the room's 15 C is unsettled, and on Bouterse's 3 cents per degree a 15 C bore would sound about 36 cents lower still. On the crescendos the first register now starts at a higher pressure: 187, 185, 279 and 177 Pa on F4, A4, Bb4 and B4 (before: 103, 103, 78 and 99), and each crescendo is loudest at 104 to 204 Pa, in a higher mode of the pipe under its first register. An alto recorder built from the published measurements of one real baroque alto (a Bressan recorder of the Frans Brueggen collection, as tabulated by Jan Bouterse): the bore of its three joints, the thumb hole and six finger holes, the window, the labium and step, and the windway length; then every length is scaled by 409/440 (0.92955), the ratio of the a1 = 409 Hz that Bouterse prints for this alto to 440. The windway height is not published for this instrument; the pages take 0.98 mm, measured by Blanc on a Zen-On alto, a modern Bressan copy at A440, not this instrument. The jet's convection speed (0.3 of the jet speed) is measured, by de la Cuadra and by Blanc; the flue's vena contracta (0.6) is an orifice value, not one measured at a labium. Four fingerings of the first register, F4, A4, Bb4 and B4 from Bouterse's table, are rendered as slow crescendos that choose no pressure at all, and F4 and A4 also as held notes at a pressure read from published register-jump thresholds. The scale and melody add G4, C5, D5, E5 and F5 from the American Recorder Society's alto chart, which names no recorder. C5 to F5 are blown at one player's measured pressures from Blanc's 2009 thesis, on a Zen-On Bressan alto with a machined aluminium chamfered head, not the maker's own; Blanc reports the makers Henri Gohin and Philippe Bolton judging the channel of those machined heads too low. Speaks; not graded on the site. It speaks, but it does not sound like a recorder yet: on the crescendos its first register holds from 187, 185, 279 and 177 Pa to the top of the ramp on all four, where a real Bressan alto has already jumped to its second register (at 230, 305, 505 and 490 Pa); under its first register it sounds higher modes of the pipe. Listening only: screened recordings of recorders exist in the library (84 valid clips on 18 pitches from Bb4 to E6, from several instruments, sources and licences, none of this Bressan alto), but the grader's library is built from UIowa-named files and holds none of them, so no pair is graded and nothing here claims to match a real recorder.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing pressure through the viscous windway law with the published windway length, the published window length as the jet length and the window width as the flue width, acting on a connected duct network (one jet drives the whole graph)

the published bore of the head, middle joint and foot as equal-volume cylinders (the head's oval at its area-equivalent diameter), the thumb hole and six finger holes as chimney sections on ideal junctions (chimney height from the published outer diameter and the local bore), open or closed per the published fingerings, each open hole with its inner length (the Dubos-Dalmont law at its local bore), its matching length and its series length (Garcia Mayen et al. 2021, eqs. 12 and 10; the series length is taken off the bore on each side of the hole), and the bore closed by the block behind the window

the window as an acoustic mass from Ernoult and Fabre 2017's closed form (fitted to 444 finite-element windows) for the published 12.0 x 4.6 mm cut with parallel cheeks and the labium ramp, moved from their edge plane to the window centre, in place of a textbook end correction; the 3-D potential-flow solve of the same cut still runs as the comparison; the network keeps the window's channel only as a one-sample inlet line, so no 1-D line rings across a channel whose cross modes start at 13.5 kHz
hole 7 on the foot at a derived position (24 mm below the socket rim, bracket 18 to 30 mm), open in a1, b-flat1 and b1 as the published fingerings open it

breath as the gas in the bore: exhaled breath saturated with water at 27 C with its published 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 (dry), the woodwind breath law, read from the shared woodwind breath gas pack; it lowers every passive mode 19.1 to 19.3 cents below saturated air

fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the long bore sections (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops its memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, adbb97dbb and f78078db2)

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops the open holes and the foot's open end take the compact unflanged-pipe load instead, Garcia Mayen 2021, Eq. 14, with Silva et al. 2009, Eqs. 10-11, the foot's from ae3ef2d4e, and are still heard as baffled sources), plus the window, which radiates from the outer face of the same 3-D solve on the head's rigid outer cylinder (resistance from the cylindrical-harmonic series, its static mass by Kramers-Kronig and taken out of the window mass, a passive chain of parallel R-L-C cells fitted from 20 Hz to 24 kHz within 1.9 %) in place of an authored window loss (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops that radiation's memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, 27631e7a4)
deterministic oscillation: every held note sounds the same pitch and level for another jet seed, so it is a limit cycle and not a filtered seed

the first register's pitch on the pages the site serves. Those pages play this alto with every length scaled by 409/440 (0.92955), the ratio of the a1 = 409 Hz that Bouterse prints for this alto to 440 (on 2026-11-08 it replaced 0.9067, a factor fitted to bring the pages to A = 440 on average), so the cents here are of equal temperament on A = 440. The held F4 and A4 (135 and 210 Pa) sound -64.8 and -91.7 cents. On the crescendos the first-register span read before (the 100 ms windows in the first 1.5 s, below 153 Pa, whose strongest line from 150 to 2500 Hz is within 100 cents of the passive first mode and whose level is within 40 dB of the clip's loudest 100 ms) now holds no window on F4, A4 and B-flat4 and one on B4 (+15.9 cents at about 28 Pa): the first register starts higher (see register control). Where the ramp passes 400 Pa (0.2 s windows) the crescendos sound F4 -26.6, A4 -69.0, B-flat4 -37.8 and B4 -52.6 cents (before: +25.9, -8.3, +20.1 and +6.4), where the passive first modes of the served cards are -45.9, -72.9, -37.1 and -48.7 cents (a transfer-matrix port of each card with the terms its render realised: the open holes' inner, matching and series lengths, the unflanged open end and holes, the window's computed mass and its radiation on the head's outer cylinder, the bore gas at 27 C). That 27 C is the shared woodwind breath gas: the mean bore gas of a played mouth-blown woodwind, after Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969 and Fletcher and Rossing. A played Baroque flute measured with thermocouples along its bore averaged 27.3 C in a 20.6 C room (Soubeyran, Padfield, Gohin and Spohr). Bouterse's pitches for this alto were played in a 15 C room: f1 -14.8, a1 -34.8, b-flat1 -4.8 and b1 +5.2 cents of equal temperament on a1 = 409 Hz, which this scale maps to A = 440. The held F4 and A4 sit 50.0 and 56.9 cents flat of them, and at 400 Pa the crescendos 11.8, 34.2, 33.0 and 57.8 cents flat. Whether the bore of a played recorder sits at the breath's 27 C or nearer the room's 15 C is unsettled: on Bouterse's 3 cents per degree a 15 C bore would sound about 36 cents lower. The intervals from F4: the held A4 -26.9 cents, and at 400 Pa A4 -42.4, B-flat4 -11.2, B4 -26.0, against Bouterse's -20.0, +10.0, +20.0. Nothing is added to close the gap

breath noise at the flue: the `jet_noise` row (seed 14), a pressure source at the flue jet of rms 0.0013 of the jet's rho U^2 / 2 inside the Strouhal band St_h 0.045 to 0.115, open while the flue's Re_h = U h / nu is at least 700, which this flue (h 0.98 mm, the card's air) reaches at 69 Pa. Every page clears it: F4 held at 135 Pa (Re_h 978), A4 held at 210 Pa (Re_h 1220), and the four crescendos from 0.67 s, reaching 2063 at their 600 Pa peak. The constant, band and gate come from Verge's measurement of a flue jet at a labium with a 1 mm slit (PhD thesis, TU Eindhoven 1995, sec. 5.5), not determinable below Re_h about 1700, which this flue reaches at 407 Pa: the held pages and the crescendos' first 4.07 s take that gain below its measured range. The binary has no noise tap, so the noise's own level in the clip is not read apart

The player's airway ahead of the windway (`upstream_airway`, landed as 07dc291d4e), on the Bb4, C5, E5 and F5 stops of the scale (the pages Bb4-stop, Bb4-stop-versilian, C5-stop, C5-stop-versilian, E5-stop and F5-stop): Story's measured vocal tract for /u/ (2008, Table I, 44 sections, lips first) ahead of the Weibel 1963 subglottal tree to 24 generations, with the voice cards' yielding wall on every tube. Each sample the airway's port gives the windway's foot pressure in closed form; the airway's resistance to steady flow (5.256e4 Pa s/m^3 in the receipt) holds the foot below the blowing pressure, and those stops sound 1.48 to 1.97 c lower than without it. The airway and the pipe exchange no waves: the jet's speed depends only on the foot pressure. Since ad2f27d055 the row carries `two-way` on these pages: where the open-circuit pressure at the windway is not positive, which happens in the attack on 669 samples of the 288 kHz clock, in 29 runs, to sample 1264 (4.39 ms), and on none after, the windway draws air back by its own law, signed, with the forward coefficients, a stand-in: the measured windway tapers (opening to exit area about 1.7, Bouterse 2010), so the quadratic coefficient of air drawn back lies between ρ/2 (taken) and ρ/(2 × 1.7²), and the entrance loss at the windway's chamfered exit is printed nowhere. The most air drawn back is 6.43e-6 to 9.03e-6 m^3/s. The air drawn back comes from the window side at ambient pressure, the airway stays filled with the source gas and the mixing has no model, and a sample that draws air back has no jet. One way, the windway passed no flow on 660 samples in 40 runs over the same span. On the count C5-stop gains one measure (4 to 5 of 15, and 4 to 5 by the strict ruler: partial level trajectories come inside both rulers, 16.8 to 11.9 dB), and the other five pages tie. With `two-way`, against the one-way windway on the same binary, all six tie.

The measured set's optional rows on the counted stops (2026-11-09, on the live two-way cards, one binary and host, one grading run): Bb4-stop-versilian, C5-stop, C5-stop-versilian and E5-stop play all three, `opening_losses` on every opening (the flute pages' values: C_c 1, the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it, the side holes a loss 1.2 times the sharp-edged hole of Dalmont et al. 2002), `observer_gas stokes-kirchhoff` (classical viscothermal absorption in the room air on every path to the receiver, molecular relaxation left out) and `outlet_mutual pritchard` (Pritchard 1960 as Butler 2022, Eq. 1, prints it, passive by construction); Bb4-stop and F5-stop play `observer_gas` and `outlet_mutual pritchard` without the opening losses. Over the held note (0.15 to 0.55 s) the three rows lower the pitch 0.71, 2.49 and 4.09 c on Bb4, C5 and E5 and the level 1.44, 1.02 and 1.43 dB; the two rows lower Bb4 0.38 c and 0.05 dB, F5 1.62 c and 0.23 dB. On the count C5-stop gains one measure (5 to 6 of 15: third-octave band envelope comes inside the ruler, 8.141 to 7.593 dB against at most 7.646 dB) and the other five pages tie.
physics_missing: a graded comparison on most pages: the held F4 and A4 pages and the four crescendos play Versilian sustains (The Recorder, Community Edition, Alto-440B: F3, A3, A#3 and B3 rr1, named an octave below sounding) and stay listening only. The reference screen refuses F3, A3 and B3 rr1 on measurability (the clip has no lead-in and no tail), not on a measured noise level, and no held clip grades a crescendo page, so the crescendos carry no count until a recorded crescendo is found; no open-licence recording of F4, G4 or A4 passes the screen. The scale's stops are graded where one does: C5, E5, F5 and Bb4 against Benjabola's alto (a YouTube video under the Creative Commons Attribution licence, clips re-cut from it), C5 and Bb4 also against the Versilian alto at A = 440; the D5 stop has no count, because the grader's whole-file floor refuses the reference its rule picks. None of these recordings is this Bressan alto

register control: read from the sound of each crescendo the site serves (the blowing pressure rising evenly from 3 Pa to 600 Pa over 6 s; 40 ms windows, each period by autocorrelation), the first register sounds from 187, 185, 279 and 177 Pa on F4, A4, Bb4 and B4 and holds to the last window read, at 597 Pa, on all four (on F4 the windows from 155 to 185 Pa read at half the first mode, 168 Hz). A real Bressan alto, measured on an artificial mouth, leaves its first register at F4 230, A4 305, Bb4 505 and B4 490 Pa: here the first register lasts at least 2.60, 1.96, 1.18 and 1.22 times past that ceiling, and starts only at 0.81, 0.61, 0.55 and 0.36 of it. Under the first register the pipe sounds higher modes: F4 743 Hz at 48 to 70 Pa and 1132 Hz at 85 to 149 Pa; A4 876 Hz at 52 to 111 Pa and 1273 Hz at 113 to 183 Pa; Bb4 925 Hz at 68 to 105 Pa, 1238 Hz at 111 to 169 Pa and 1568 Hz at 193 to 271 Pa; B4 901 Hz at 72 to 91 Pa and 1194 to 1208 Hz at 97 to 169 Pa. Each crescendo is loudest in that stretch (its loudest 40 ms window at 104, 130, 204 and 112 Pa), and the first register at 400 to 600 Pa sits 10.1, 10.5, 10.1 and 3.9 dB under that window (the median window). From 30 to 60 Pa the clips are 80 and 96 dB below their loudest window on F4 and A4, and 279 and 274 dB below on Bb4 and B4, at or near digital silence. The held F4 and A4 (135 and 210 Pa) sound the first mode, at 336.4 and 417.3 Hz. These reads are of the measured set the site serves from 2026-11-08: the jet_transfer auvray-2014 row with gamma 0.3, no windway row, the windway 0.98 mm, every length 409/440 of the Bressan's, and the contraction mouth loss with alpha 0.6, the vena contracta Auvray et al. 2014 print in Table I from orifice data (Ingard and Ising 1967), not measured at a labium (it was 0.9, the top of the range Auvray et al. 2012 explored, not a fit). On the cards served before 2026-11-08 (every length 0.9067 of the Bressan's, gamma 0.4, contraction 0.9, windway 0.960 mm) the first register sounded from 103, 103, 78 and 99 Pa and held to 444 and 480 Pa on F4 and A4, then jumped to the pipe's second mode, and to 597 Pa on Bb4 and B4. Diagnostic renders of those earlier four crescendos (2026-11-08, one row changed at a time, not served) named the cause. With the mouth's contraction loss off (`mouth_loss none`) the first register sounds from 99, 99, 76 and 97 Pa to the top of the ramp on all four fingerings: the upper edge comes from the Auvray jet loop with no mouth nonlinearity, and only the contraction row, then at 0.9 (not a fit), pulled F4 and A4 down to 444 and 480 Pa. With the convection ratio gamma 0.3 in place of 0.4 the first register starts 1.60, 1.79, 2.31 and 1.72 times higher (165, 185, 179 and 171 Pa; the jet delay alone scales by 1.78) and the higher modes under it move up with it: the lower-edge modes belong to the jet loop and move with gamma. The `jet_transfer nolle-price-2015 long-channel 0` row does not lock to the pipe on these cards: every fingering sounds near 400 Hz. A developing windway (the published 61.5 mm) cannot be combined with this card's Auvray jet row, which takes the exit speed U = sqrt(2P/rho) and refuses every windway law (flue_loop.rs:1637-1639, auvray_jet.rs:36-37); on the 600 Pa crescendos the slit's own developed-flow bound (Re_Dh 1760, bernoulli_aperture/developing.rs:208) refuses it first. The tin whistle's pages blow through other rows (a developing slit windway, the forced-Bickley jet response, contraction 0.6), so their registers are no evidence about these

the windway: its height is not published for this alto (only its length): the pages take 0.98 mm, measured by Blanc (PhD thesis 2009, sec. 6.2.1) on a Zen-On alto, a modern Bressan copy, not this instrument. Blanc gives that recorder's low G as 392 Hz (sec. 6.2.2), so it is an A440 instrument and its 0.98 mm enters the A440 pages unscaled (0.98 x 440/409 = 1.054 mm at this alto's own size); its curved, crescent-shaped opening, the direction of its roof, the chamfers and the taper of its section are unknown, and the recipe has a straight rectangular slit. The pressure-to-jet-speed map and every register claim depend on the height, and a sweep of the published bounds has not been made

labium offset: DERIVED, not measured. The published step and edge give the edge underside 0.27 mm on the bore side of the jet centreline at the windway height (Blanc's Zen-On 0.98 mm at A440, x 440/409 = 1.054 mm at this alto's size), and the jet splits at the middle of the 0.25 mm face: +0.1479 mm on the pipe side (face ends +0.02 to +0.27 mm; the windway-height bounds move it from -0.225 to +0.425 mm); jet angle zero. The served pages, every length 409/440 of the Bressan's, carry it as +0.1374 mm, 0.35 of the Auvray row's Bickley half-width at the labium (2h/5 = 0.392 mm). That row splits the jet's flow as H b U (1 + tanh((eta - y_off)/b)) (auvray_jet.rs:10-12, flue_loop.rs:1780-1782), so the offset sets how much of the even harmonics the jet makes. Read on the clips the site serves (0.2 s Hann windows; the un-parity index of Auvray et al. 2015 is 10 log10 of the odd harmonics 3, 5 and 7 over the even 2, 4 and 6, in power): on the crescendos where the ramp passes 400 Pa, H2 sits below H1 by 24.9 dB on F4, 15.4 dB on A4, 17.6 dB on B-flat4, 30.3 dB on B4, and the index is -12.8, -9.2, -7.7, -7.1 dB; at 140 Pa all four now sound the pipe's higher modes (see register control), so no first-register figure is read there; on the held F4 (135 Pa) and A4 (210 Pa), H2 is 31.0 and 23.8 dB below H1 and the index -4.2 and +7.5 dB. Auvray et al. 2015 measured about -2 dB at 140 and 400 Pa on a Zen-On Bressan head with a cylindrical foot (a comparison only: not this instrument). The jet's swing at the labium is not read on these renders
the second and third registers: the thumb hole is a fully open or closed hole; the half-closed thumb hole that raises the register is not modelled, so only first-register fingerings are rendered

pitch: hole 7's position is derived, not measured (bracket 18 to 30 mm); the finger holes have no undercutting, and the closed holes no matching volume or series length (the open holes carry their inner, matching and series lengths, which are open-hole forms); the labium edge height is inherited from the windway height, measured on another recorder (see the windway) (an edge at the bore or 1.25 mm above it moves every note by about +10 or -9 cents, passive); the measured bore is the tabulated maximum of a shrunken, slightly oval boxwood joint (the head taken at the oval's area-equivalent diameter, the midpoint of its published 0.2 to 0.4 mm)

the jet: the `jet_transfer auvray-2014 0.3 0.3` row (Auvray, Fabre and Lagrée 2012; Auvray, Ernoult, Fabre and Lagrée 2014): receptivity in phase with the mouth's acoustic velocity at the flue exit, flat growth exp(beta W/h), pure convection at gamma U, a Bickley profile of half-width 2h/5 at the labium and Verge's distance (4/pi) sqrt(2hW) between the two injection points, with U = sqrt(2P/rho). It replaces the interim slot-jet card's band chain, convection ratio and demonstrator displacement gain of 90 (flue_loop.rs:1612-1617, 1775-1778, 1966-1969); of that card only the onset seed (1e-6 of the jet speed, flue_loop.rs:2163) still enters, and its Reynolds band is only reported block by block (flue_loop.rs:2403), not enforced. beta 0.3 is the value Auvray et al. 2014 print in Table I, which holds over a few jet thicknesses and was validated on one Zen-On Bressan alto at W/h about 4, not measured on this instrument. gamma 0.3 is measured: de la Cuadra (PhD thesis, Stanford 2005) finds the perturbations on a jet from a long channel convected at about 0.3 of the jet's centre speed (Figs 2.14a and 2.17a, Re 200, Str_h 0.05 to 1.1), and Blanc (PhD thesis 2009) takes c_p = 0.3 u_j. At the recorder's own Strouhal number (0.018) de la Cuadra's Fig. 5.4 reads 0.32 near Re 1070, falling to 0.25 near Re 2000 and 0.20 to 0.22 from Re 2650 to 6050; the row keeps one gamma and no Re-dependent value is added, while these pages run at Re_h 978 (F4 held) to 2063 (600 Pa). The cards carried 0.4 until 2026-11-08, the value of Auvray et al. 2014 Table I, which that paper attributes to the experiments of de la Cuadra and Blanc; both theses print 0.3 for a long channel (de la Cuadra 0.5 for a 1 mm one), and this windway is long (61.5 mm). On these cards W/h is 4.36, the growth to the labium 3.70, the half-width 0.392 mm and the injection distance 3.69 mm. The row takes its own exit speed and so refuses every windway law (auvray_jet.rs:36-37): no windway loss is in these pages
a spectrum and attack like a real recorder: the first register lasts far past the real instrument's ceiling (see register control), and no chiff or edge-tone noise is modelled

the gas beyond the breath law: the CO2 fraction is the published one for exhaled breath, not measured in a played recorder; no temperature gradient along the bore, and the published pitch was measured in rooms at 15 to 27 C (about 40 cents between them); whether the bore of a played recorder sits at the breath's 27 C, as the pages take, or nearer the room is unsettled
native verification beyond one fingering at two mechanics clocks and two jet seeds on a few files

Openings that hear each other: the open holes and the foot's open end radiate apart. Tried on the cards served before 2026-11-08 (every length 0.9067 of the Bressan's, gamma 0.4, contraction 0.9, windway 0.960 mm) with every opening hearing every other free-field, after the travel time between them (`outlet_mutual free-field`), every page and scale or melody note with two or more holes open (the A4 held page; the A4, Bb4 and B4 crescendos; A4, Bb4, C5, D5, E5 and F5 in the stops) was refused before rendering, because with these loads the row is not passive: the real part of the openings' impedance matrix has a negative eigenvalue from the lowest frequencies up to 73 to 138 Hz with three openings, and up to 2.1 to 3.1 kHz with five to seven. The time step is not the cause: the exact free-field term with the loads' continuous form fails on the same notes. Each compact unflanged-pipe load's resistance falls short of a free-field monopole's by a share that grows with the square of frequency, and three or more openings in a line, closer together than a wavelength, radiate so nearly as one source that the matrix has less than that to spare. G4, with the foot and one hole open 78.2 mm apart, passes; it is not a page, so the row stays off the recorder

Openings that hear each other, weighted by their own radiation: tried on the cards served before 2026-11-08 (every length 0.9067 of the Bressan's, gamma 0.4, contraction 0.9, windway 0.960 mm) with the free-field term between every pair of openings scaled by the square root of the two openings' own radiation resistances over a free-field monopole's (`outlet_mutual pritchard`; Pritchard 1960 as printed by Butler 2022, Eq. 1, with the geometric mean for unequal openings), which is passive with these loads by construction, every page and scale or melody note rendered. The row lowered the A4 held page, the A4, Bb4 and B4 crescendos by 0.7, 0.7, 0.4 and 0.2 c. A4 and B4 already sit flat of the recording, so the gap grew: 27.7 to 28.4 c on the A4 held page, 19.2 to 19.9 c on the A4 crescendo, 5.8 to 6.0 c on the B4 crescendo. Bb4 sits sharp and its gap shrank, 10.0 to 9.7 c, but the mean error of H2 to H12 against the recording grew, 15.07 to 15.27 dB. The mean error went 12.21 to 11.65 dB on the A4 held page, 9.936 to 9.941 dB on the A4 crescendo and 5.43 to 5.54 dB on the B4 crescendo. No page gained on both, so the row stayed off those cards. The half-space form of Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard (2013, Eq. 16), twice the free-field term, is set aside: with these unflanged loads it is not passive even for two openings On the measured set (2026-11-09, on the live two-way cards) the row rendered on the four counted stops, every opening pair beyond the ten-sample gate: the held pitch fell 0.38, 1.43, 2.03 and 1.62 c on Bb4, C5, E5 and F5 and the level 0.05 to 0.23 dB, and all six counts tie, so all six stop pages now carry it (see the measured set's optional rows under physics present). The held and crescendo pages and the D5 stop have not been tried with it on the measured set.

Separated flow at the openings: the flow leaving each open hole and the open end separates and loses its kinetic energy, a loss in series with each opening's own radiation (`opening_losses`, Δp = ρQ|Q|/(2(C_c A)²)). Tried on the cards served before 2026-11-08 (every length 0.9067 of the Bressan's, gamma 0.4, contraction 0.9, windway 0.960 mm) with C_c 1 on every opening: the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it (C. R. Mécanique 332:299-304, Eq. 3, c_d = 2 for a thin-walled unflanged end), the side holes at the row's ceiling of 1, a loss 1.2 times the one Dalmont et al. 2002 print for a sharp-edged hole (Acta Acust. united Ac. 88:567-575, K_h = 0.5, as quoted by Szwarcberg et al. 2024, JASA, Sec. III.2.1, which is C_c 1.096): a C_c above 1 would be pressure recovery, which this row's full-head loss cannot represent. Every page rendered. The mean error of H2 to H12 against the recording grew on all six pages: 12.21 to 12.60 dB on the A4 held page, 9.61 to 9.81 dB on the F4 held page, and 9.94 to 12.34 dB, 15.07 to 16.67 dB, 5.43 to 12.12 dB and 11.94 to 12.44 dB on the A4, Bb4, B4 and F4 crescendos. The pitch moved by 0.5 c or less: the A4 held page went 0.5 c flatter, further from the recording; the A4 and B4 crescendos went 0.4 and 0.3 c sharper, closer to it; the Bb4 and F4 crescendos went 0.5 and 0.2 c sharper, further from it; the F4 held page moved less than 0.01 c.
